title: Unified SDK error model: actionable exceptions, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a single, language-idiomatic error model across Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go). Goal: provide deterministic error classification (retryable vs terminal), stable error codes, and actionable human-friendly messages plus developer-facing fields for telemetry and automated handling. This ticket covers the design, cross-SDK contract, examples for common flows (sync calls, streaming responses, long-poll retries), and a plan for a gradual rollout with feature flags and backwards-compatible deprecation notices.
background: Multiple SDK teams have implemented ad-hoc error shapes: Python raised model-specific exceptions, TS returned typed errors in callbacks/promises, and Go returned wrapped errors with different sentinel values. This causes client confusion, inconsistent retry loops, and flaky streaming behavior (partial streams followed by opaque errors). Recent customer incidents (high-retry storms, broken graceful cancellation) highlighted the need for a single source of truth for errors and retry semantics. Related tickets: ENG-8219, ENG-9341.
acceptance_criteria: A cross-language error spec documented in SDK RFC (code, category, retryable:boolean-as-string, explanation, docs_url)
Python, TS, and Go SDKs expose language-idiomatic types: Python Exceptions (RedwoodError family), TS Error subclasses or typed Error objects, Go error wrappers with Is/As helpers
Clear retry guidance and helper functions in each SDK (is_retryable(error) helper; automatic idempotent-only retries for safe endpoints)
Streaming ergonomics: SDKs deliver errors mid-stream with a consistent terminal/Error event shape and provide cancel() semantics that stop server-side work where supported
Migration guide and deprecation plan published (including compatibility shim for older clients)
Unit + integration tests covering transient network failures, server 5xx, model-timeout, malformed response, and token quota errors
Telemetry tags emitted for error.code and error.category for routing/alerting in Redwood Console
design_notes: Core design principles: (1) Machine-readable code namespace (e.g., RWD_Auth_InvalidToken, RWD_Runtime_KVCacheMiss), (2) High-level categories: auth, quota, rate_limit, transient_network, server_error, client_error, model_error, streaming_error, validation, internal, cancelled, timeout, not_found, permission, billing, config, upgrade_required, unsupported, deprecated, io, parsing, backoff_required, retry_exhausted. (3) Retry policy encoded on error as 'retryable' flag (string "true"/"false") and 'retry_hint' string like 'immediate','exponential','none'. (4) Streaming model: final terminal event MUST include an error object when stream ends abnormally; SDKs should surface partial data plus the error where possible. (5) Errors carry docs_url pointing to human guidance and remediation steps. (6) All SDKs implement isRetryable(error) helper and backoff helper using retry_hint.
implementation_plan: Write SDK RFC and publish in docs/references/sdk-error-model.md
Implement python exception hierarchy in sdk/python/redwood/errors.py and update client to raise RedwoodError subclasses
Add structured error payload mapping in TS SDK; ensure thrown Error has error.code and error.retry_hint properties
Implement Go error types using errors.Join wrappers and provide helper functions IsRetryable(err) and Code(err)
Add e2e tests with network fault injector and streaming cancellation scenarios
Roll out feature flag to beta customers; gather telemetry for misclassified errors
Deprecation grace period (90 days) and migration helpers in CHANGELOG
progress_updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with SDK owners (Asha, Marcus, Lina). Agreed on category taxonomy and that error codes should be namespaced with RWD_. Assigned RFC draft to Asha.

2026-02-18: RFC first pass posted: docs PR #1842 (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1842). Feedback from TS lead (Lina) to prefer Error objects over subclassing for Promise ergonomics — follow-up discussion scheduled.
2026-02-25: Python prototype implemented in branch sdk-python/unified-errors. Raises RedwoodAuthError, RedwoodTransientError, RedwoodStreamingError. Marcus opened PR #6201 for initial review.

2026-03-03: TS approach converged: use Error subclassing with added properties (code, retry_hint) to keep instanceof checks working while preserving V8 stack shapes. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/913.

2026-03-09: Go API design finalized: use sentinel Code(...) helper and sentinel vars for common errors plus errors.As helpers. Lina and Marcus paired on the Go test harness for streaming cancellation.

2026-03-12: Added streaming test vectors for partial-token delivery and terminal error event. Discovered an edge case where proxy drops connection without error payload — decided to classify as RWD_Network_Aborted with retryable=false and include guidance in docs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Breaking changes for existing SDK users if we change error shapes. Mitigation: implement compatibility shim and feature flag; preserve old behavior unless opt-in.
Risk: Different language idioms make exact parity impossible. Mitigation: focus on consistent surface contract (code, category, retry_hint, docs_url) rather than exact types.

Risk: Misclassification of retryable errors leading to retry storms. Mitigation: start with conservative defaults (fewer automatic retries), add telemetry to detect mislabels, and allow config override per-client.
Risk: Partial stream data loss on abrupt disconnect. Mitigation: SDKs should expose partial result plus final error when available and document server guarantees.
Risk: Increased bundle size for JS SDK. Mitigation: keep error metadata minimal (code as short token, docs_url opt-in) and tree-shake helpers into a separate small package.
notes_for_reviews: Reviewers: focus on the retry_hint semantics and the streaming termination event shape. Check that Python exceptions preserve original stack and that Go helpers work with errors.Is. Also validate telemetry keys are present: telemetry.error_code and telemetry.error_category.
